# August 27, 2026

## Summary {.unnumbered}

**The K_init consensus sweep was extended from 8 spot values to the full K_init=2..20 grid, and now
includes BIC and an ELBO-style joint log-likelihood alongside ELBO and external C-index.** A new
helper, `compute_joint_ll_bic()`, combines the genomics reconstruction term already tracked during
CAVI with a Cox partial log-likelihood recomputed post-hoc from the returned fit, and derives a BIC
(`df = K_init·(n+p+1)`, charged by the CAVI starting K, not by ARD's K_eff). See §1.

**The four criteria do not agree, and that disagreement is reported rather than resolved.** ELBO and
BIC both prefer K_init=3; external C-index prefers K_init=12, though K_init=7 through 20 mostly sit on
a plateau around C≈0.627. K_init=7 is kept as the presented recommendation — survival-active count is
stable at 2 from K_init=7 up — but the full curves and a per-K table are shown alongside it rather
than only the recommendation, to make the disagreement visible. See §1.

**The multi-cohort simulation was rewritten to select K the way the real-data procedure now does:**
an over-specified K_init pruned by ARD, instead of handing the model the oracle true K. Recovery,
specificity, and held-out C-index are flat across K_init=6/12/20 in every scenario — a clean,
well-powered confirmation (15 seeds) that over-specifying K and trusting ARD costs nothing relative to
knowing the true K. See §2.

**A secondary question — does over-specifying K_init increase the false-positive rate on non-signal
factors — softened under more seeds, which is itself the finding worth recording.** At 5 seeds it
looked like a clean improvement; at 15 seeds the improvement in the realistic scenario is directionally
consistent but not significant (paired p=0.07), and an apparent improvement in the negative-control
scenario turned out to be seed noise (flat at both seed counts once averaged properly). See §2.2.

**The 2026-08-27 lab meeting deck is built and dropped the loadings predictor (Lβ) from the narrative
entirely.** Only the projection predictor (YF)β is presented going forward. See §3.

## §1 — K_init consensus sweep

Extended `results/benchmark_sim/run_k_init_sweep.R` from 8 spot values (5,6,7,8,9,10,15,20) to the
full K_init=2..20 grid, and added a joint log-likelihood / BIC column via a new
`code/compute_bic.R::compute_joint_ll_bic()`. The genomics term is read from the fit's own
`history$elbo_proxy` at its final iteration (not a naive `tail()`, which is wrong for any fit that
converges early), plus the Gaussian normalizing constant the per-iteration tracker omits. The survival
term is recomputed post-hoc from the fit's *returned* `EF`/`EBeta` — matching exactly what external
prediction does — rather than read from a stale in-loop value that predates the post-loop
sign-correction step.

| K_init | Survival-active | Genomics-only | Dead | Kept | ELBO | BIC | External C |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 | 1 | 2 | 0 | 3 | −806,636 (best) | 1,575,712 (best) | 0.594 |
| 5 | 3 | 1 | 1 | 4 | −808,404 | 1,581,651 | 0.596 |
| 7 | 2 | 2 | 3 | 4 | −810,540 | 1,614,174 | 0.627 |
| 9 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | −810,421 | 1,623,321 | 0.627 |
| 12 | 2 | 3 | 7 | 5 | −820,752 | 1,662,678 | 0.630 (best) |
| 20 | 2 | 3 | 15 | 5 | −847,800 | 1,767,584 | 0.627 |

ELBO and BIC both prefer the smallest K_init tested (3); BIC's complexity penalty (~13,100 per unit
K_init here) makes this unsurprising once K_init climbs into double digits. External C-index prefers
K_init=12, but the plateau from K_init=7 onward is wide — most points in that range sit within a few
thousandths of each other. Two isolated dips (K_init=11 and 13) are visible against their neighbors,
consistent with the single-seed CAVI factor-collapse artifact already documented for other K values,
not a new failure mode.

**Decision:** K_init=7 is kept as the presented recommendation for the same reason it has been kept
before — the survival-active count (2) is stable there and beyond, and it is reachable from a single
fresh fit rather than a warm-start procedure. The full sweep is presented alongside it specifically so
the disagreement between criteria is visible to the audience, not smoothed over into a single number.

**Two open items were raised in review and are tracked in ROADMAP.md, not yet acted on:** whether the
ARD retention thresholds themselves (PVE>1%, |β̂|>0.001) need a literature grounding and a sensitivity
sweep — `beta_threshold` in particular was reverse-engineered from this model's own coefficient scale,
not drawn from a citable source — and whether a fully Bayesian K-selection alternative (a prior on K
itself) is worth scoping as a longer-term replacement for the current post-hoc consensus.

## §2 — Multi-cohort simulation under ARD

`results/multi_cohort_sim/run_multicohort_sim.R` previously fit every arm at the oracle true K (K=6
in every scenario) and compared 5 arms including the loadings predictor. Rewritten to 2 arms
(the projection predictor, and the unsupervised EBMF→Cox baseline) fit at three K_init settings:
K_init=6 (the oracle value, retained only as an internal reference point) and K_init=12/20, mirroring
the real-data over-specify-then-ARD-prune procedure.

The K_init=6 setting, re-run through the new script, reproduced the original June results almost
exactly (e.g. hybrid-scenario held-out C-index 0.815 vs. 0.815) — a useful confirmation that the
rewrite changed nothing about the underlying fitting, only which K values get compared.

Across K_init=6/12/20, recovery correlation, specificity-classification accuracy, and held-out C-index
are flat in every scenario. Over-specifying K and trusting ARD to prune costs nothing relative to
knowing the true K in advance — the core validation this exercise was designed to produce.

### §2.2 — A false-positive-rate trend, and a lesson about seed count

A natural follow-up question: does giving ARD more unnecessary factors to work with increase how often
it falsely calls a non-signal factor survival-active? At 5 seeds, the answer looked like a clean "no,
if anything it improves": the hybrid scenario's false-positive rate dropped from 0.45 (K_init=6) to
0.20–0.25 (K_init=12/20), and the negative-control scenario dropped from 0.067 to 0.033.

Re-running at 15 seeds (a `--n-seeds` override was added to the runner rather than changing the shared
seed list in `config/globals.yml`, which several other simulation scripts also read) told a more
measured story. The hybrid-scenario drop is still there directionally (0.35→0.22→0.27) but a paired
t-test (same seeds, K_init=6 vs. 12) gives p=0.07 — not conventionally significant. The
negative-control scenario's apparent improvement turned out to be an artifact of only 5 seeds: at 15
seeds it is flat at 0.10 across every K_init tested.

The honest summary is two-layered: the primary metrics (recovery, specificity, C-index) give a
well-powered null result with no caveats needed; the false-positive-rate question gives a directionally
consistent but not-yet-significant trend, worth watching rather than reporting as settled. Both are
presented that way in the 8/27 deck rather than collapsing to a single "ARD helps" headline.

This also lines up with a separate discussion with advisors about the 8/21 finding that ARD can
over-count survival-active factors in simulation: a small, non-zero coefficient on a non-signal factor
contributes minimally to the risk score in practice, so over-counting in this sense is a lesser concern
than it might first appear, independent of whether the false-positive *rate* itself trends up or down
with K_init.

## §3 — The 8/27 lab meeting deck

`presentation/walther_lab_meeting_08_27_2026/` is built from the 6/18 deck as a template, not a diff
against it — the loadings predictor (Lβ) is dropped from the methods, results, comparison table, and
appendix entirely, and the K-selection story is rewritten as the two-stage ARD framework described in
§1. The cohort-membership-indicator extension moved out of Methods into Future Directions, reframed as
a forward-looking multi-cohort/multi-modality direction rather than a tested-and-rejected result.

The external two-step baseline was reframed to the fairest comparison available (EBMF→Cox, K=40, LASSO
stage 2) rather than the smaller/unregularized baseline the June deck used; the headline pooled
bootstrap difference (+0.026, 95% CI [0.0002, 0.0498]) was verified to reproduce directly from paired,
patient-aligned risk scores before it went on a slide, rather than taken on faith from prior prose.
